summary: Erich Herold was an Indologist who earned his Ph.D. at Charles University in 1947, studying under Oldřich Friš and Vincenc Lesný. He served as director of the Náprstek Museum from 1959 to 1970.

Philosopher Erich Rudolf Jaensch studied at Breslau, Göttingen (PhD ~1908), and Strasbourg. He held professorships at the University of Halle (1912–1913) and the University of Marburg (from 1913), which he founded in 1933.

Erich Wolff was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at the University of Hamburg and later at Heidelberg University (1924–1930), where he completed his Ph.D. under the supervision of Max Walleser.

Erich von Voss was a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He studied at the University of Tartu and completed his Ph.D. at the University of Leipzig (~1902–1906). From ~1906 to 1917, he taught German and Greek at Petrischule.

Erik Braun, a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies, studied at Harvard University under doctoral supervisor Janet Gyatso and teachers Jonathan Evans, John Okell, and Saw Tun. He held posts at Harvard (attested 2010) and Virginia (attested 2026).

Erik Erikson studied at the University of Oxford. During his career, he held positions at the University of California, Berkeley (~1939–1950), the University of Pittsburgh (~1951–1960), and Harvard University (~1960–1970).

Classical historian and archaeologist Erik Gren studied at Uppsala University (~1923–1941). He served at Uppsala University Library as Assistant Librarian in 1931 and became Privatdozent of classical history at Uppsala University in 1941.

Erik Haarh studied at Copenhagen (mag.art. 1953, Ph.D. ~1969) under Pallis, Grønbech, Tuxen, and Barr, and under Tucci. A scholar of Tibetology, linguistics, and religious studies, he held posts at Copenhagen and Aarhus University (professor 1983–1987).

Erik J. Hammerstrom is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology. He earned his Ph.D. at Indiana University Bloomington (attested 2010) and served as assistant professor of religion at Pacific Lutheran University (attested 2016).

Linguist Erik Johan Tammelin studied at the University of Helsinki (M.A. ~1886, Ph.D. ~1890) and the University of Jena under Berthold Delbrück. At the National Board of Education, he became chief inspector (1894) and secondary schools department head (1918).

Erik Pema Kunsang is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He became director of Rangjung Yeshe Publications around 1980 and served as resident teacher at Rangjung Yeshe Gomde Denmark starting around 1981.

Erik Reenberg Sand is a scholar in Indology and religious studies. He held a position at the University of Copenhagen from ~1981 to 2015 and worked as a cataloguer of Hindi and Panjabi manuscripts for the Wellcome Trust (attested 1995).

Erik Zürcher was a scholar of Sinology and Buddhist studies who earned his PhD at Leiden University (~1947–1959), also studying under Demiéville, Bagchi, Chavannes, and Duyvendak. He directed Leiden University (1961–1993) and co-edited T'oung Pao (1975–1992).

Linguist and historian Erik-Jan Zürcher completed his BA and PhD at Leiden. He held posts at Radboud University Nijmegen (1977–1997), the International Institute of Social History, the University of Amsterdam, and became a professor at Leiden University in 1997.

Erika Forte works in archaeology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Buddhist studies. She served as a research associate at Ruhr University Bochum from 2018 to 2019 and is attested as a professor at the Italian School of East Asian Studies.

Erika Sandman is a scholar of linguistics, Sinology, and Tibetology. She completed her Doctor of Philosophy at the University of Helsinki between 2007 and 2016, and she holds a post at the University of Helsinki.

Sinologist Erling von Mende studied at Hamburg, Freiburg, Bonn, and Cologne (PhD 1969, Habilitation ~1979). In 1983, he was appointed professor of Sinology at the Free University of Berlin, serving until 2007.

Ermenegildo La Terza studied at the University of Naples Federico II under Michele Kerbaker (~1884–1888). A scholar of Indology and linguistics, he taught Sanskrit and comparative linguistics at Naples, and Latin literature at the University of Messina (1923–1924).
Archaeologist and historian Ernest Arthur Gardner studied at Gonville and Caius College from ~1880 to 1884. He later held an academic post at the University of London from 1924 to 1926.

Ernest B. Havell, who worked in history, archaeology, and Indology, studied at Reading School and the Royal College of Art. He served at the Government Colleges of Art in Chennai and Kolkata, and in the Indian Education Service (1885–1906).
